title: What It Takes: Johnny Cash (2/4)
titleZh: 成功的條件：強尼・凱許 (2/4)
summaryZh: 強尼・凱許回憶四歲時聽到火車歌曲，從此立志要在廣播上唱歌。
source: VOA Learning English (public domain) — What It Takes

sentences.text: These are the people Johnny Cash wrote and sang about for 40-plus years.
sentences.zh: 這些就是強尼・凱許四十多年來寫歌、唱歌的對象。

sentences.text: He lent his entirely original canyon of a voice to the lonesome and the lost, the dispossessed and the disillusioned.
sentences.zh: 他用那如峽谷般獨一無二的嗓音，為孤單的人、迷失的人、被剝奪的人和心灰意冷的人發聲。

sentences.text: In 1993, Gail Eikenthal sat down to talk with Johnny Cash.
sentences.zh: 一九九三年，Gail Eikenthal 坐下來和強尼・凱許聊了聊。

sentences.text: It was 10 years before his death.
The first time I knew what I wanted to do with my life was when I was about four years old.
sentences.zh: 我第一次知道自己這輩子想做什麼，大概是四歲的時候。

sentences.text: I was listening to an old Victrola playing a railroad song.
sentences.zh: 當時我正聽著一台老式留聲機播放一首鐵路歌曲。

sentences.text: The song was called Hobo Bill's Last Ride.
sentences.zh: 那首歌叫〈Hobo Bill's Last Ride〉。

sentences.text: Hobo Bill, a railroad bum, was fighting for his life.
sentences.zh: 歌裡的流浪漢比爾是個扒火車的遊民，正在為自己的性命掙扎。

sentences.text: And I thought that was the most wonderful, amazing thing that I'd ever seen, that you could take this piece of wax and music would come out of that box.
sentences.zh: 我覺得那是我見過最美妙、最神奇的事：拿一片蠟盤放上去，音樂就會從那個盒子裡跑出來。

sentences.text: From that day on, I wanted to sing on the radio.
sentences.zh: 從那天起，我就想在廣播上唱歌。

sentences.text: Johnny Cash's musical dreams took root on a cotton farm in rural Arkansas during the darkest days of the Depression.
sentences.zh: 強尼・凱許的音樂夢，是在經濟大蕭條最黑暗的日子裡，在阿肯色鄉下的一座棉花田生根的。

sentences.text: But it wasn't just Jimmy Rogers or the other singers coming out of the family's radio that inspired him.
sentences.zh: 不過啟發他的，不只是從家裡收音機傳出來的 Jimmy Rogers 和其他歌手。

sentences.text: I grew up in the 40s, and I heard all these great speeches like Winston Churchill.
sentences.zh: 我在四〇年代長大，聽過很多精彩的演說，像是邱吉爾的演講。
